description: Level 2 (Grumpstone Ridge) bankruptcy-by-overspend playthrough. Named for a $250k win, but `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright (locked) and, under queued, vehicle-gated drilling, the $150,000 budget cannot fund the 12-person roster staffed:true adds through the first drilling wait: BANKRUPTCY fires at tick 176 (agent occupancy on, #1262). #1313: the mine freezes the instant the level ends, so the blasts, contract acceptances and later patterns this file used to play on top of an already-lost game can no longer run; the file now pins the opening (3 surveys, fleet, ramp, drill order) up to the bankruptcy and asserts the frozen state afterwards (cash and tickCount unchanged).

steps.description: #553: staffed:true added -- cash:150000 sits on this new_game, not on the campaign start below, because that command fails outright (grumpstone_ridge is tier-2, locked on a fresh campaign, Finding #59), so it never replaces this state and a cash: on it would be discarded with the rest of the command. staffed:true hires and equips its own free crew before any assertion here: employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1), #2 blaster, #3-5 drivers, vehicle #1 drill_rig, #2 debris_hauler, #3 rock_digger, #4 rock_fragmenter -- free, not deducted from cash, which is why employeeCount is already 5 here instead of 0. All four vehicles come unmanned (driverId: null); vehicle driver 1 1 immediately below crews the free rig with the free driller, since drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action and nothing drills without a driver aboard. The extra $100,000 over the sandbox default is what the three-vehicle fleet at step 36 needs, same as before -- but see the pattern-1 drill-wait step further down for what that budget can no longer survive once drilling takes hundreds of ticks instead of zero.

#553: crews the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) with the free driller (employee #1) staffed:true just hired -- unmanned, the rig is a mesh no queued drill_hole action can ever start against. #921: the Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls were removed from the DOM entirely -- runs as a bootstrap command instead.

issue #585: the repo-wide commandOutcome audit found this file's 4 contract-deliver steps refused with 'Not enough <ore> in storage: 0.0 kg available' no matter how many ticks preceded them. Direct trace (createGameEngine + runCommand replay) found the real cause: this file never once builds a freight_warehouse anywhere in its 187 steps -- and HaulingTask.ts's requestHaulFragment (the only code path that ever increments storedMassKg/collectedOre, called from both the manual haul and the auto-dispatch haul_debris action alike) hard-requires findNearestActiveBuildingOfType(..., 'freight_warehouse', ...) to resolve a depot before a hauler will so much as pick up a fragment. With none built, storedMassKg traced flat at 0.0 for 600+ ticks past blast 1 regardless of wait length -- not a timing gap, a missing prerequisite. Fixed by building one here instead of the second rock_digger this file also bought: sandbox-traced across the full 187-step file, vehicle #5 (that purchase; staffed's own #3 already covers rock_digger and sits idle the whole run too) never got a driver or left 'idle' -- this file drills no ramps (no dig_ramp_segment command anywhere in it), the only task type a rock_digger claims, so the purchase was dead weight both before and after this fix. Swapping it for a $15,000 T1 warehouse ($35,000 cheaper than the rock_digger it replaces) at (2,8) -- clear of all 4 drill patterns' footprints (confirmed via trace: patterns span roughly x10-37/z15-46) and close to the vehicle spawn row (z:2) -- actually improves the cash trajectory (was $3,278 after all 3 buys, now $38,278) rather than worsening it, and (also confirmed via trace) leaves blast 1's own death toll and timing untouched, unlike every warehouse tile tried closer to the drill patterns, which perturbed blast 1's own navgrid-dependent hole-completion timing and its death count. Moved from (2,8) to (6,0) for #1008: the footprint-flatness check now enforced on placement found (2,8)'s ground uneven. (8,6), the nearest flat 4x4 site, sits one tile inside the x10-37/z15-46 drill-pattern box and blast 1 demolished the warehouse there (re-traced); (6,0) is the next-nearest flat site, clear of that box on both axes, and re-tracing confirms the warehouse survives blast 1 there. Interaction is a real build-panel click (this step lands at tick 32, well before the tick-132 bankruptcy overlay that blocks every later click in this file) -- a command-only interaction here would have let command mode and interaction mode silently diverge on world state from this point on, exactly what .claude/rules/scenario-defs.md warns against. The vehicle-buy-assign step right after this one now assigns driller #8 to vehicle #6 (drill_rig), not #7 -- see that step's own note.

Was an unmarked command step that overdrew: the Fleet panel disables a dealership row on `cash < def.purchaseCost` (setTierButtonAffordable, FleetPanel.ts), so no click could buy this while the console bought it anyway. The console now refuses an unaffordable purchase and the run is funded for the fleet, so this is a real click on the debris_hauler tier-1 row ($25,000). awaitUsable is the affordability assertion. issue #585: re-opens the Fleet panel explicitly -- the previous step now builds a freight_warehouse (Build panel) instead of buying a second rock_digger (Fleet panel), so Fleet is no longer already open here the way it was before.

#553: vehicle #7 (staffed claims #1-4; rock_digger and debris_hauler above claim #5-6). This is the driller's-second-rig this file already needed under the old semantics (Finding #59 -- bought but its own driller never licensed) -- now driller #8, licensed above, crews it via vehicle driver 7 8 below, giving this file 2 concurrent driller/drill_rig pairs for the drilling wait that follows.

#553: driller #8 crews the second drill_rig -- 2 concurrent driller/drill_rig pairs (staffed's #1/#1 and this pair) for the drilling wait below. issue #585: vehicle #6, not #7 -- the earlier build-freight_warehouse step now really builds one via a real click too (not just command mode), so the second rock_digger this file used to buy never happens in either mode, and the second drill_rig is #6 in both. #921: the Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls were removed from the DOM entirely -- runs as a bootstrap command instead.

#953: a blasted bench is no longer terrain a worker walks off -- its face is a six-voxel drop, and pathfinding now refuses that step instead of letting haulers stroll over the edge. Access to the pit floor is a dug ramp, exactly as gameplay-navmesh describes it, so this level digs one from the rim at (24,14) down into the block it is about to blast, before the blast rather than after (cash is still positive here, and the excavation crew has the three tick-150 steps below to finish it). Without it every haul_debris action queued by the first blast targets a cell no employee can reach: traced flat at one stored fragment for 2400 ticks, and the four contract-deliver steps below all refuse with 'Not enough stored material'. #1151: origin moved from (24,12) to (24,6) and depth set explicitly to 7 (was the unspecified default 8) -- length 13 now satisfies length >= ceil(depth * 1.8), keeping every per-column step within NAV_MAX_SLOPE_RATIO, while floor((length-1)/length * depth) = floor(12/13*7) = 6 keeps the ramp's actual deepest carved column at the same six-voxel drop the surrounding blast (drill depth:6) and this description already assume -- the old length:7/depth:8 pairing reached that same 6 via floor(6/7*8). The corridor's own footprint roughly doubles in length, so its total excavated volume is larger than before; if a future scenario run finds the ramp not fully dug by the point haul_debris needs it, widen the tick-150 budget below rather than re-shorten the ramp back below the new slope minimum.

steps.description: #553: sandbox-measured -- this is where the mine's math actually breaks. staffed:true's free composition adds 5 more salaried employees on top of this file's own 7 hires -- a 12-person roster costing ~$7,570 per payroll cycle (Payroll transaction, every ~10 ticks, Finance.ts) against a $150,000 budget that used to only have to fund 7. After hiring, surveying and the 3-vehicle fleet, cash sits at $3,278 -- already under BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD ($5,000, balance.ts) before a single tick of this wait runs. BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (100) later, 'BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized.' fires at tick 176 (state.bankruptcy.bankrupt / state.levelEnded flip to true, state.levelEndReason to 'bankruptcy', Bankruptcy.ts) -- inside this very first tick chunk, 205 ticks before the 2 driller/drill_rig pairs actually finish sinking this 24-hole pattern (tick 337) and long before blast 1 ever fires. Nothing in the engine stops a `tick` command from continuing to run a level after levelEnded flips (a genuinely pending EVENT, like the Explosive Tariff below, is the only thing that ever halts one), so the mine keeps operating -- legally seized, crew still working -- for the rest of this file.

#553: resolves the Explosive Tariff event that cut this tick call short at tick 140 (108 of 150 requested) -- politics_explosive_tariff option 0 pays the $20,000 tariff in full (fixed, RNG-free delta). CI finding, this PR (#586): was role:player driving `resolveEventIfPending`'s real click -- state.levelEndReason has read 'bankruptcy' since tick 176 (8 ticks before this event pends), and the event dialog's own overlay class (`.bs-confirm-overlay`, EventModal.ts) sits at z-index 600, far below `--bsx-z-menu` (9999) that LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay has owned since tick 176 -- same class of bug as the Charge/Sequence/blast steps further down this file, just on a dialog instead of a panel, and reached earlier because this event happens to pend this late. Every other 'event choose 0' step in this drilling wait stays role:player safely because `resolveEventIfPending` no-ops (no click at all) when nothing is genuinely pending; this is the one step in the wait where an event really is pending at the moment it runs, so it is the one that actually reaches `resolveEventIfPending`'s bare `page.click('#bs-event-dialog .bs-event-choice')` -- which has no `describeUnclickable` wrapper, so Puppeteer's own unnamed 'Node is either not clickable or not an Element' surfaced instead of a diagnosis. Converted to guard + expect.blocked, command run directly so cash still drops by the tariff. Update: EventModal now also defers behind LevelEndScreen once the level has ended (UIManager.update, matching BlastReportModal's own fix for the same z-index gap) -- its .bs-event-choice buttons are never rendered at all in that state rather than rendered-but-covered, so probing for them reports 'absent', which expect.blocked itself rejects as unprovable (scenario-goal.ts/interaction-driver.ts). Reassigned to #bs-event-dialog, the dialog's own outer overlay -- created once in EventModal's constructor and left in the DOM at display:none, so it is the one still-present, genuinely-hidden control left to assert against.
